citations.quote: AI4CE is an open-source project at the Technical University Darmstadt in cooperation with Parametry.ai that operationalises bottom-up system generation for CubeSats.

In this paper, an initial architecture is described, together with a curated component database (108 parts across 23 component types in 8 sub-systems) and a set of evaluation functions by which component-, sub-system-, and system-level performances are scored in mission context.

All entries in the component database are transcribed from manufacturer data sheets mapped by hand to a list of supported parameter names and SI units, since automated scraping was not found reliable.

Four generation methods — random, brute-force, genetic optimiser, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) — are integrated into a unified pipeline with consistent constraint handling, result storage, and comparison tooling.
Source code and artefacts are made available at https://ai4ce.space.
An increasing market of commercial CubeSat components has enabled a much larger design space than ever before for any kind of satellites - but especially for CubeSats.

citations.quote: Assumed the performance of a system/ component combination can be measured via established engineering textbook heuristics based on data sheets alone, as outlined in [1], each combination of components will be given a score between -1 and 1.

The simplest solution to finding a suitable combination out of multiple possible, would be test all possible combinations in a brute-force manner and pick the one design with the highest rating. The strong exponential growth of the design space makes this infeasible in a system design scenario.
From this, two main questions can be derived: 1) how to evaluate a set of components forming a CubeSat system? 2) how to find the best-fitting combination within a given design space?

AI4CE is designed to find answers to the following research questions (RQ): RQ1) How to use DRL to generate preliminary system designs (bottom-up system generation) on component level ? RQ2) What is needed to enable bottom-up system generation? RQ3) What is the potential of AI-based bottom-up system generation?
